question.text: A single turn current loop in the shape of a right angle triangle with sides <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>12</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>13</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> is carrying a current of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math>. The loop is in a uniform magnetic field of magnitude <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>75</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></math> whose direction is parallel to the current in the <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>13</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> side of the loop. The magnitude of the magnetic force on the <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> side will be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi><mn>130</mn></mfrac><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> is _______.

solution.text:
Here, B=0.75 T

The magnitude of magnetic force on the 5 cm side is FAB=i×lABBsinθ           angle between AC & AB

=2×5100×0.75×1213

=9130 N

Hence, the value of x=9.
